mission.title: A Key with No Lock
mission.description: Track the fugitive General through his last combat units and the Exiles who shelter him.

npc.say: I knew we shouldn't have agreed to help the General. This is his fault!
Agent Pace is waiting for you, {player}.
Is this some kind of practical joke? Where's my secretary?

phase.briefing:
With the destruction of his base on the Earth's surface, the General has been forced into hiding in the Matrix.
Zion's rescue of Sati, made possible by our crippling of the General's systems, has resulted in the restoration of normal weather patterns within the simulation.
As we have already eliminated the General's primary Matrix stronghold, and his data network, he has few places to hide here, and a rapidly dwindling supply of combat units. I am sending you to one of those units now, {player}. The General must be located and terminated.

enter.say: We've got some commando action in there.

done.say: I bet that kind of message just works wonders for troop morale.

phase.briefing:
His tactics are growing increasingly desperate. Surely the General realizes that he is merely delaying the inevitable.
Forward scans along his projected route have detected programs believed to be under the control of the Merovingian. Their presence can be no coincidence. It is believed that they may be more...forthcoming than the General's own units. You are to capture one of the Exiles, and then await further instructions.

enter.say: Got Exile signals in there, all right. We'll have to keep an eye out for one we can nab.

done.say: Okay, get him out of there.

talk.say: What do you want? The Merovingian will deal with the General. You'll see!

objective.text: Lead Buda out of the area

near.say: Buda there looks like as good a weak link as any. Get rid of his buddies and haul him outside.

phase.briefing: Operative, you are to take the captured Exile to Agent Pace. She will handle extraction of the required data.

enter.say: Whoa, I wonder what Pace is gonna do to that guy.
Picking up her signal in there.

done.say: The Merovingian will take care of it...
Good. Let's see what Pace wants us to do now.

talk.say:
Grazie, {player}. I am prepared to obtain data concerning the General's whereabouts from the subject. It should not be overly...difficult.
While I am performing this task, you will lead the two programs you just saw outside, and await directions to the strike location.

done.say: Darn it, I wanna know what she's gonna do to that guy.
You will have the data shortly, operative. I will see to it...personally.

objective.text: Lead Wilson Vyse and Cordell Lange out of the area

phase.briefing: Coordinates are incoming from Agent Pace now, operative. Continue pursuit of the General and his forces at the indicated location.

enter.say: I still wanna know what she did to that guy.
I'm reading more Merv signals in there.
The next door is secured. Looks weird... Haven't seen code quite like that before. The computer in that room controls access, but it looks secure too. We'll probably need some kind of access code.

done.say: Yep, we'll need an access code for that.

objective.text: Get the access code from the Elite Guard

done.say: Okay, try the code in the computer.

objective.text: Enter the access code in the computer

done.say: Whoa, what... The whole area just blinked. What is going... Hm, and the computer's reset. Door's open, though.

talk.say:
Thank goodness! The lock jammed somehow. I tried calling out, but nobody answered. Sounded like it must have been hell getting the bolt forced open from out there, but--
Wait... Who are you? What's going on here?

done.say: Wait a second... I wasn't picking up that bluepill before. Something weird is going on here.

Aw, crud. That's what it was. The door's normal now--too normal. They changed something. Wherever that door used to go, it isn't going now, which means that this is a dead end. The ol' switcheroo from the Merv.

mission.finish: It appears that the Merovingian has given the General access to his system of "back doors," operative. We do not currently have access to these areas, and the routines required to access them are known to change frequently. Nevertheless, we must now devote the necessary resources to penetrate this system. The General will not be allowed to remain at large within the simulation.
